rules: Any liquid asset: stock, crypto, or leveraged/inverse ETF
Rotate each 6:30am CT run — sell yesterday, buy today's best
Leverage matched to conviction; asymmetric payoff preferred
Hard stop at entry; spot-crypto-only on weekends

positions.name: Bitcoin
positions.catalyst: US equity market CLOSED (Saturday) — spot crypto is the only eligible instrument. BTC's flow picture just inflected: spot Bitcoin ETFs took in ~$510M across three sessions and +$265M on 7/10, snapping a 10-day, $2.73B outflow streak. The Senate returns to Washington next week and is expected to unveil final CLARITY Act market-structure language 'within days'; Polymarket odds of it being signed in 2026 jumped to 40% from 30-35% a week ago — a live headline catalyst that can land on thin weekend liquidity. BTC is pressing $64.4K, the level it failed at on Monday; a clean break opens the June 15 peak of $67,250 (+4.9%). Fear & Greed reads 23 (extreme fear) with leverage restrained — positioning is light into the CPI print on 7/14.
positions.driver: BTC is the only crypto with the fresh catalyst attached to it. ETH is the explicit flow LOSER — spot ETH ETFs are still bleeding while BTC's flipped positive, ETH/BTC sits near a 10-month low, and ETH is 60% off its peak vs BTC's 48%. Buying the higher-beta asset whose own flows are negative is anti-asymmetric, so ETH was rejected despite the beta. SOL (-5.2% on the day, no catalyst) was rejected on momentum. That leaves BTC: the deepest, lowest-vol book in crypto (best downside protection, per the objective), sitting on a defined technical trigger with a defined target, into extreme-fear positioning where the pain trade is up. Not a chase — BTC is +~2% on the day and +2.6% on the week, far inside the no-chase band. Spot, unleveraged: weekend liquidity is thin and leveraged crypto ETFs (BITX et al.) don't trade today, so leverage isn't available even if conviction warranted it.
positions.risks: Weekend crypto is thin and gap-prone in BOTH directions — a liquidation cascade on low depth can overshoot. BTC has failed at $64.4K once already this week; a third rejection likely means a retest of the $60-62K shelf. The CLARITY catalyst is headline-dependent and could just as easily slip again (it already blew past the July 4 deadline). A hot CPI on 7/14 delays Fed cuts and pressures all risk assets; Middle East escalation is a live tail. Structural bear regime remains intact — BTC is ~49% off its Oct-2025 high of $126,198. Hard stop $60,281.51 (-6%), set deliberately TIGHTER than the 10% crypto default: it sits just under the $60K shelf that held in late June, so it triggers only on a genuine thesis break rather than on noise, maximizing downside protection.
